name: Abu al-Atahiya
bio: Abu Ishaq Isma'il ibn al-Qasim was born at Ayn al-Tamr, near Kufa, in 130 AH (748 CE), grew up in Kufa and began by selling earthenware jars, before settling in Baghdad and rising high in the favour of the Abbasid caliphs. He is counted among the leading poets of the new generation, with Bashshar and Abu Nuwas, and is best known for his poems of renunciation, wisdom and counsel, many of whose lines became proverbs. He composed with great ease and was said to turn out a hundred or a hundred and fifty lines a day. When he gave up poetry for a time, the caliph al-Mahdi had him jailed until he took it up again. He died in Baghdad in 211 AH (826 CE).
